_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's tech-meetup-announcement template (studio/templates.py make --spec). Its film is projects/tech-meetup-announcement (local: the hosts' logos are third-party), pulled from kitcut.ai film studio-20261002-165325-bxo5ja with studio/template_from_film.py: AI Agents Speakeasy, LiveKit and Modal's happy hour at LA Tech Week 2026 (Wed Oct 14, 6-9 PM, Santa Monica; tech-week.com). Its facts were one object at the top of film.js, moved into content.json and proven pixel-identical at 13 moments.
title: Tech meetup announcement
description: A 30-second announcement for a tech meetup, music only: the tech week or series tags in, the hosts' logos land side by side, the meetup's name builds letter by letter under a neon arch, who it is for and what kind of evening it is, what it is not (struck through) and what it is in up to three beats with icons, a ticket card with the day, the time and the place, and the hosts again with the call to RSVP, the link and the hashtag. A dark art-deco speakeasy look, every word on screen.
author: KitCut
example: Our Rust meetup in Austin, Thursday Nov 12, 6-8 PM at Capital Factory, talks and pizza. Our logo is attached.
brief:
A 30-second meetup announcement with no narration, on one 120 bpm clock that never moves (a beat .5 s): the hosts' logos (1-3.7 s), the name under the neon arch (4-8.7 s; it then shrinks into the header), who it is for and the format pill (9-13.7), the not-list struck through (14-16) and the beats (16.5-20.7), the ticket card (21-25.7) and the end card (26-30). score.json and sfx.json are the film's, timed to that clock: keep them.

Everything the film says is content.json (SK.DATA.content). series (the tech week, conference or series, up to ~20 characters, upper case; "" for none) and edition (the year, or ""); hashtag (or ""). name: the meetup's name as its page writes it (it is set in capitals and fitted: one line, or two balanced lines past ~22 characters). hosts: 1 to 3 {name, logo, col}: logo is a picture key of a logo that reads on a near-black ground (white or light type): call template_pictures(logos=[...]) with the hosts' logos in order and use the "light" key it answers (logo-1-light...); col is that host's own accent colour (its brand's), used for its accents. join: the mark between logos (keep "×"). audience: who it is for, one sentence up to ~60 characters, and audienceAccent: the words of it to colour (or ""). format: the kind of evening in a few words ('Invite-only happy hour', 'Two talks + pizza'). not: 0-2 short lines the event itself says it is NOT ('No sales pitches.'); [] when the event says nothing like it -- never invent one. beats: 1-3 {text, icon}: what happens, from the event's page, up to ~26 characters each; icon is 'cocktail', 'canape' or 'talk' (drawn by the film) or a kit icon (mic, play, users, chat, calendar, star, heart, bolt, globe, money, pin...). day (WED), date (OCT 14), time (6–9 PM), place: the neighbourhood or the venue and city, up to ~28 characters; never a private address the event hides. cta: how to sign up, as the event says it ('RSVP on Luma', 'Free · Register on Meetup', 'Apply to join'); link: the shortest address that opens the event, without https:// (up to ~30 characters). colors: the film's palette (ground, panel, interior, amber, text, soft, onCta); keep the dark ground and the warm amber unless asked -- the hosts' colours are the accents.

Find the facts on the event's own page (Luma, Partiful, Meetup, Eventbrite, the host's site, or the tech week's calendar) and the hosts' logos on their brand pages (the picture tool); never invent a date, a time, a place or a beat. A talk night, a demo night or a workshop: rewrite the beats for it and leave not empty if the page has no such line. A meetup with more than three hosts: the three the event names first.
